name: Astra Microwave Products Ltd
title: Astra Microwave Products Ltd - 532493 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 turnover of INR1,157 crores in line with guidance; order book INR2,141 crores standalone and FY27 top-line growth reaffirmed at 15-20%.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 turnover of INR1,157 crores, in line with the start-of-year guidance, with operating cash flow of INR370 crores versus minus INR99 crores a year earlier. Q4 billing was INR490 crores (up 16% YoY) and Q4 fresh orders were about INR530 crores, taking the standalone order book to INR2,141 crores at 31 March 2026. Management reaffirmed FY27 top-line growth of 15-20% and guided to roughly INR1,600 crores-plus of orders in FY27, with a board-approved in-principle demerger of the space, meteorology and hydrology business. The call leaned heavily on a long-range "near-triple turnover in 4.5-5.5 years" narrative, with proprietary IP products and the Su-30 upgrade positioned as upside rather than included in the numbers.

segments.name: Radar
segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 60% of FY26 revenue and is expected to be about 45% of FY27 orders/mix. Shipborne radar systems were handed to DRDO for final testing.

segments.name: Space and meteorology
segments.commentary: Contributed about 16% of FY26 revenue and is expected to be about 25% of FY27 orders. Management said space is about 10-15% of sales, and defence satellite subsystems were completed in Q4.

segments.name: Electronic warfare and missile
segments.commentary: Expected to be about 25% of FY27 orders, driven by Su-30 EW DCPP role (Angad) and active seekers for couple of missiles, with orders expected in 2-3 years.

segments.name: ARC (Astra Rafael Comsys JV)
segments.commentary: FY26 orders INR546 crores and sales INR360 crores. Management targets at least 50% growth in both orders and sales in FY27, with INR200 crores of FY27 order visibility and sales above INR600 crores expected.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth reaffirmed at 15-20%, with potential for much stronger growth over coming years.
FY27 order inflow visibility of about INR1,600 crores-plus; planned sales of INR1,300-1,400 crores (about 15-20% growth), with 40% from R&D and 60% from production.
Roughly 25% of FY27 expected orders from R&D programmes, balance from production orders.

Management expects to nearly triple turnover in 4.5-5.5 years (around FY30-FY31) driven by about five or six programmes (QRSAM, Uttam radar, Su-30 Virupaksha, Su-30 Angad, JV business and electronic mines), excluding export and IP-product upside.
Capex to remain around INR40-50 crores per year; no incremental capex beyond normal run-rate expected; working capital needs to rise with volumes but are expected to be met within sanctioned limits.

Management indicated FY26 margin (about 55% as stated, likely gross margin) should be sustained; JV EBITDA guided at 18-20% with at least about INR20 crores share of profit on INR600 crores JV revenue.
capex_capacity: Annual capex of about INR40-50 crores to augment existing capacity; no additional capex beyond normal run-rate expected for the 3x plan.
Demerger of space, meteorology and hydrology business approved in principle by the board; detailed scheme expected within weeks.
Miniaturisation work underway for radars using in-house components; digital array radar and photonics radar subsystems delivered to DRDO.
First NCNC demo of proprietary product planned within the current quarter; multiple Astra-branded IP products targeted before Diwali.
demand_pricing: Management cited about 75% of India's defence capital acquisition budget allocated to domestic companies and FY26 defence exports above INR38,000 crores.

Export margins: exports to ARC are RF content of SDRs co-developed with Rafael; management said gross margin on these is about 40-45%, versus single-digit margins on build-to-print (BTP) business, which the company has exited.
Uttam radar order: negotiations with HAL at final stage; order expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27.
QRSAM: BEL expects its contract by about June 2026; Astra has started receiving small quantities for FOPM; production orders expected 3-4 months after BEL's main contract.
Su-30 radar (Virupaksha AAAU): development to complete in next 2-3 months; DRDO qualification possibly FY28, then user qualification and about 2-3 years to production orders.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins sustain given rising space and export mix, and what are the exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are to wholly owned subsidiary ARC with higher value add (RF portion of SDRs co-developed with Rafael), with gross margin near 40-45%. Space subsystems for a defence satellite contributed decently in Q4 and similar orders are expected from ISRO and defence. Management said margins are a function of order mix and may vary.

qa_highlights.question: How much more capex is needed for the 3x revenue target, and will working capital improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR40-50 crores a year with no additional capex beyond normal run-rate. Working capital will rise with volumes but should be funded within sanctioned limits; receivables realisation is expected to continue, so finance cost should be similar to FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Given space order book share has shrunk, how does margin mix look?
qa_highlights.answer: Space is about 10-15% of sales, so a lower space order share should not hurt overall margins. Management said FY26 margin was about 55% and the aim is to sustain it, with guidance at the top end and margin numbers possibly slightly lower to avoid disappointment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MMIC dependency and sourcing position?
qa_highlights.answer: No issues encountered in MMIC production or development. Most active devices in subsystems are sourced from the in-house MMIC division, and the company is now promoting MMICs to domestic and international customers.

qa_highlights.question: Has the total addressable market (about INR28,000 crores FY26-FY28) changed?
qa_highlights.answer: The total accessible market is unchanged, but programme timing has slipped, so the opportunity window moves from FY28-FY29 to FY30-FY31 due to budget and priority delays.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and business scale for the Su-30 upgrade programmes?
qa_highlights.answer: Radar qualification likely in FY28 with user qualification about one more year; EW (Angad) development expected to complete in about one year; production orders are expected 2-3 years after that, with DRDO timing not controlled by Astra.

qa_highlights.question: Why was JV profit only about INR1 crore and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR1 crore figure was for Q4; full-year JV share of profit was about INR8 crores after tax. Around $2 million of forex provision and ongoing R&D weighed on profit. JV EBITDA is projected at 18-20%, implying at least about INR20 crores share of profit on INR600 crores revenue, with management calling INR20 crores a minimum.

risks_watch: Programme timing slippage from DRDO and government-driven budgets; the TAM window has shifted to FY30-FY31.
Su-30 radar and EW programmes are still in development; production orders depend on DRDO and user qualification and may take 2-3 years after qualification.
Quarterly margin variability depends on order mix; management warned of possible variations.
Working capital needs will rise with volume growth despite improved receivables realisation.
ARC profitability hit by forex provision (about $2 million) in FY26; JV profit conversion is well below the earlier 10-12% PBT framing.
Consolidated vs standalone order book distinction (INR2,600 crores vs INR2,141 crores) and the demerger structure need clarity when the scheme is published.
Uttam (HAL) and QRSAM (BEL) order timing (Q2-Q3 FY27 and post June 2026) are key near-term catalysts.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term strategy and the three-fold growth narrative, but cautious and hedged on specific timing of DRDO and Su-30 orders, repeatedly noting that delays are possible. Management also described the INR20 crore JV profit as a minimum and guided margins to the top end with some caution.
key_quotes: We are very much a tier-1 systems company.
not a single rupee from these future proprietary IP-led opportunities has been factored into our near threefold growth aspiration over the next five years.
the margins delivered by the company in the current year is about 55%.
This is probably as best as it gets, if I may say so.

growth.why: FY27 top-line growth reaffirmed at 15-20% (planned sales INR1,300-1,400 crores) backed by a INR2,141 crore standalone order book and ~INR1,600 crore-plus FY27 order visibility, though the 3x long-range plan rests on programmes (Uttam, QRSAM, Su-30) with timing slipping to FY30-31 and no new capacity additions beyond INR40-50 crore annual capex.
